etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Old French vacant, from Latin vacans.

quote.citation: 1892, E.K. Pearce, “Tweed Side”, in The Gentleman's magazine, page 171:
quote.text: Below and to rearward circles the Tweed, silver grey on a dark brown field. Beside its low banks no tourists linger, vacant hangs the quivering bridge; down the narrow lanes no carriages come pressing over a succession of waving hills […]
